page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u2i-c1m8.large is a virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is provisioned with 2 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. The system provides 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing a high memory-to-vCPU allocation of 8.0 GB per virtual core. Hardware acceleration is not present, with zero dedicated GPUs assigned to the instance.

Storage and networking resources rely on external and virtualized cloud infrastructure. The instance features no local storage, requiring attached network block storage for persistent data requirements and operating system volumes. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth rate of 2 Gbps. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included with the baseline configuration.

The 1:8 compute-to-memory ratio provides significant memory capacity relative to the small CPU count. This configuration is cost efficient for workloads requiring substantial in-memory caching or working datasets without demanding high multi-threaded compute density. Workloads that fit this profile include in-memory databases, Redis caches, lightweight relational databases, and background ETL processes handling medium-sized memory resident datasets.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u2i-c1m8.large is an x86_64 virtual server instance configured with 2 dedicated Intel Xeon vCPUs clocked at 2.7 GHz and 16.0 GB of system memory. Operating under the KVM hypervisor, it delivers an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, offering substantial memory capacity for smaller-scale deployments. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or GPU acceleration, depending on remote block storage solutions for disk operations and providing a network baseline of 2 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Because of its expanded memory density relative to the modest processor allocation, this server type is functionally aligned with memory-heavy operations that do not saturate high core counts, such as caching nodes, in-memory key-value databases, and lightweight data staging pipelines.
